title: Preflight Simulator + Dynamic Rollback Windows for Private Control Plane Upgrades
creator: Priya Narayanan
description:
Goal: Build an automated preflight simulation harness and a dynamic rollback-window component integrated into our Terraform/IaC upgrade flow for private (VPC) control plane version promotion. This ticket implements an orchestration layer that runs a synthetic workload simulator against canary control plane instances, evaluates key SLO-aligned health signals, and calculates a timeboxed dynamic rollback window (DRW) based on observed metric confidence and drift.

Why: Current staged canary flows rely on static windows and manual signal inspection which causes inconsistent upgrade safety and longer incident MTTR for private customers. A simulator-driven preflight plus a DRW will reduce human toil, catch regression risk earlier, and enable safer automated promotions when signals are strong.

Scope:
- Terraform modules: extend existing upgrade modules to provision ephemeral canary tiers with simulator traffic generators and shadow networking (no customer traffic ingress).
- Preflight simulator: a lightweight harness that replays representative request mixes (generation, chat, embeddings) with KV cache warmup phases to exercise hot paths (batching, kernel selection).
- Health evaluation engine: run threshold & statistical checks across latency P95/P99, error-rate, model-token-consistency (structural outputs), KV-cache-hit-rate, and resource contention (GPU SM/PCIe).
- Dynamic Rollback Window (DRW): compute a probabilistic confidence interval for stability (e.g., 95% CI on delta metrics) and map it to a timeboxed window that determines how long an automated promotion may proceed before requiring manual approval if anomalies appear.
- Integration: wire simulator and evaluation into our control plane promotion pipeline (Terraform + orchestration state machine). Add a post-check step that writes gating verdicts to the upgrade state and emits logs/metrics to the console.
- Runbook & observability: dashboard template + alert rules for canary verdicts, DRW expiration, and rollback triggers. Add a playbook for manual override.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Terraform module change can create a temporary canary tier and destroy it cleanly via terraform apply/destroy.
2) Simulator can produce replay traffic and warm KV caches deterministically; run completes within the preflight budget (default 15 minutes).
3) Health evaluator computes signals and a DRW value and writes a JSON verdict artifact to the upgrade state bucket.
4) Orchestrator honors the verdict: when confidence >= threshold, promotion proceeds; when not, promotion halts and notifies on-call.
5) Unit + integration tests for simulator, evaluator, and Terraform changes exist in repo and pass in CI.
6) On a staged rollout to two internal tenants, we observe no more than 5% deviation in production-like metrics during promotion compared to baseline.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We use synthetic workloads to simulate worst-case and nominal traffic mixes; synthetic cannot catch every semantic regression (e.g., hallucinations), so we maintain paired eval prompt-sets for content regressions as a separate gate.
- DRW uses statistical heuristics rather than full Bayesian forecasting initially for implementation velocity; if effective, we'll iterate to probabilistic forecasting in a follow-up.
- Ephemeral canary infra will be cost-accounted to the upgrade job; default run frequency is per-version promotion only (not per minor patch) to limit cost.

Terraform changes (high-level):
- modules/upgrade/canary.tf -> new resources: redwood_canary_instance_set, redwood_canary_network_attachment (private), null_resource.simulator_job (provisioner triggers).
- variables: canary_size, simulator_profile, preflight_timeout, drw_confidence_threshold.
- outputs: canary_verdict_bucket, canary_instance_ids, simulator_run_id.

Operational metrics to monitor:
- preflight.simulator.duration_seconds
- preflight.simulator.kv_warm_hit_rate
- preflight.health.latency_p95_delta
- preflight.health.error_rate_delta
- preflight.drw.confidence_score
- controlplane.promotion.rollback_count

Safety thresholds (initial):
- latency_p95_delta <= +15%
- error_rate_delta <= +0.5% absolute
- kv_hit_rate >= 90% after warmup
- confidence_score >= 0.95 to auto-promote

Rollout plan:
1) Spike PR implementing simulator and TF modules behind feature flag. Code review + security check.
2) Deploy to staging and run against internal canonical tenants for 2 week A/B window.
3) Iterate thresholds and DRW heuristic with observed telemetry.
4) Pilot on 3 small private customers (opt-in) with manual approval required.
5) GA with opt-out knob and monitoring/alerting configured.

Notes on tenant isolation:
- Canary networking must not route customer traffic. We will use tenant-fenced ephemeral VPC attachments and ensure egress policies block customer cluster endpoints.
- Logs and artifacts are written to a dedicated upgrade-state S3 path with restricted IAM.

Next steps (short):
- M1 (this week): PoC simulator harness + simple TF module to create/destroy canary nodes.
- M2 (next 2 sprints): Health evaluator + DRW computation + integration into promotion pipeline.
- M3: Staging pilot, threshold tuning, finalize runbook.
